chapter: Lionel Hampton and life on the road
title: Lessons from Lionel Hampton and Jack McDuff
summary: On the road as a young white player he learned toughness and no room for weakness in the Hampton and McDuff bands.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Earlier you were talking about going to New York and you landed the Lionel Hampton gig and worked with Brother Jack McDuff I think, what kind of things did you learn from those guys, if anything?

A lot. Well with Lionel Hampton and Jack McDuff, both, I mean, just what they’ve done for me, I learned how to be a man. Because there was no room for weakness. You know, when you’re in a safe environment, maybe you’re weak sometimes and you get let off the hook. When you go on the road, you know being a young white kid going out on a bus with people that don’t look like you, it was an experience, it was a great experience. And in the beginning it wasn’t always friendly. But at the end it was a beautiful experience. And just about everybody that was on that band, and I wasn’t the only Italian or Irish guy on the band, but we were the minority on that band. And that was a good thing for us. That was a really good thing for us. Because I was forced to play my best at all times, or I could be ridiculed very easily. Now that doesn’t mean that — everybody lived in that role, not just me, it was everybody that was there. But I had never been in an environment where it was that rough around the edges. And that was the best thing for me. It was the greatest thing I could have — I don’t think I would have got that with Buddy Rich or Woody Herman, although I would have loved to play with both of those bands because of the greatness of those bands, I would have learned a lot musically. But there were things socially that I learned with Lionel Hampton that really were great for me.
That’s interesting, that sort of self-policing there by keeping the standard high.
Keeping the standard high, and no room for weakness basically. There was no sympathy happening. And I had just moved to New York. I was there less than a year when I got the gig.
